documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital ED, visit 07/21/2026, 19:30.

CC: painful sores in the genital area.

HPI: 26F with two to three days of painful vulvar sores, now with burning on urination, fevers at home and tender lumps in the groin. No prior episodes. No meds. NKDA.

Exam: T 38.4, other vitals normal. Uncomfortable. Bilateral tender inguinal adenopathy. Vulva with several clustered vesicles, some running together, on a red base. No other rash.

Tzanck smear of an unroofed lesion: multinucleated giant cells.

Assessment: primary genital herpes simplex infection.
Plan: acyclovir 400 mg PO three times daily x10 days, started tonight, Rx sent. Sitz baths for comfort. Follow up with gynecology in the next few days; referral info given. Return for urinary retention or worsening.

Copy to primary care physician.

documents.title: ER visit last night
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, I wanted you to know I went to the ER last night and they said it's genital herpes. They started me on acyclovir and told me to see gynecology, which I have on Friday. I'm honestly really freaked out. I don't need anything right now, I just didn't want you to be surprised.

documents.title: RE: ER visit last night
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Iris, thank you for telling me, and I'm sorry you're dealing with this. It is very common and very manageable, and the first episode is usually the worst. Keep taking the acyclovir for the full course. I'll look at the ER and gynecology notes when they come in. After your gynecology visit, let's set up a time to talk through any questions that are left. Message anytime before then.

documents.title: Gynecology Visit
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
Outside gynecology practice. Date of service 07/24/2026.

Reason for visit: follow-up of genital ulcers after ED evaluation on 07/21.

History: 26-year-old seen in the emergency department three days ago with painful genital sores, fever, dysuria and tender groin nodes; clustered, coalescing vesicles on an erythematous base were noted and a Tzanck smear showed multinucleated giant cells. Started on acyclovir there. Pain is a bit better. She is very anxious and embarrassed. Her questions today: whether she must take medicine for the rest of her life, whether she can still have children, and what this means for her partner. She is in a new monogamous relationship.
Past history: sexual assault in 2022, followed by an acute stress reaction.
Medications: acyclovir only. Allergies: NKDA.
Family: mother with generalized anxiety disorder, father with hypertension.

Exam: afebrile, vitals normal. Lesions are partly healed, crusting, no new vesicles.

Assessment: primary genital HSV infection, improving.

Counseling, at length:
- Finish all 10 days of acyclovir.
- Recurrences, if any, are usually milder. They can be treated as they happen, or she can take a daily suppressive medicine. Neither is required for life; it is her choice and can change over time.
- This does not affect fertility. When she plans a pregnancy she should tell her obstetric provider, who would offer suppressive medicine in late pregnancy to protect the baby at delivery.
- Her partner can be offered testing through their own clinician. Avoid sex while sores or tingling are present, and use condoms in between.
Written information given. Return as needed or with a recurrence.

cc: primary care physician
